s0003.literal: Xu Ling, styled Zijian; his younger brother Xiaoke
s0003.idiomatic: Xu Ling, styled Zijian; his younger brother Xiaoke

s0004.literal: Xu Ling, styled Xiaomu, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
s0004.idiomatic: Xu Ling, styled Xiaomu, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

s0005.literal: His grandfather Chaozhi was Administrator of Yulin under Qi and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Outside the Body under Liang.
s0005.idiomatic: His grandfather Chaozhi had been administrator of Yulin under Qi and an outside-body regular attendant of the scattered cavalry under Liang.

s0006.literal: His father Chi was Rongzhao General and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard under Liang; posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
s0006.idiomatic: His father Chi had been a Rongzhao general and left commandant of the heir apparent's guard under Liang; posthumously he was made palace attendant and grand mentor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.

s0007.literal: His mother, the Lady Zang, once dreamed that five-colored clouds transformed into a phoenix and alighted on her left shoulder; afterward she bore Ling.
s0007.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zang, once dreamed that five-colored clouds turned into a phoenix and settled on her left shoulder; soon after, she bore Ling.

s0008.literal: At the time the monk Baozhi was called a man of the Way in the world; when Ling was several years old his family brought him to call on him, and Baozhi stroked his crown and said, "A stone qilin from heaven.
s0008.idiomatic: The monk Baozhi was held in his day to possess the Way. When Ling was only a few years old his family brought him to call. Baozhi laid a hand on his crown and said, "A stone qilin from heaven.

s0009.literal: " The Guangzha monk Huiyun often sighed over Ling's early attainment and called him a Yan Hui.
s0009.idiomatic: " The Guangzha monk Huiyun often marveled at how soon Ling came into his own and called him a Yan Hui.

s0010.literal: At eight he could compose literary pieces.
s0010.idiomatic: At eight he could compose literary pieces.

s0011.literal: At twelve he mastered the meanings of Zhuangzi and Laozi.
s0011.idiomatic: At twelve he had mastered Zhuangzi and Laozi.

s0012.literal: When grown he ranged widely through historical records and was skilled in disputation.
s0012.idiomatic: Grown, he ranged widely through histories and was quick and forceful in debate.

s0013.literal: In the second year of Putong under Liang, the Prince of Jin'an was made General Who Pacifies the West and Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians; Editorial footnote marker 1. his father Chi was the prince's advising officer, and the prince also brought Ling in as military aide on the Pacify-the-Miao staff.
s0013.idiomatic: In Putong year 2 (521), the Prince of Jin'an was made general who pacifies the west and colonel pacifying the barbarians. [1] His father Chi served as the prince's advising officer, and the prince also brought Ling onto the Pacify-the-Miao staff as military aide.

s0016.literal: Collation variant: [three] year; adopted reading: In the second year the Prince was established as heir apparent, Editorial footnote marker 2. the eastern palace set up academicians, and Ling was chosen for the post.
s0016.idiomatic: (three)/In the second year the Prince was established as heir apparent; [2] the eastern palace set up academicians, and Ling was chosen among them.

s0017.literal: He was gradually promoted to Clerk for Revenue in the Masters of Writing.
s0017.idiomatic: He rose by degrees to clerk for revenue in the Masters of Writing.

s0018.literal: He went out as magistrate of Shangyu; the censor-in-chief Liu Xiaoyi and Ling had long borne a grudge, and on rumor he impeached Ling for corruption in the county, whereupon Ling was dismissed.
s0018.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Shangyu. Censor-in-chief Liu Xiaoyi, who had long borne a grudge against him, impeached him on rumor for corruption in the county, and Ling was dismissed.

s0019.literal: After a long while he was recalled as staff officer in the Prince of Nanping's establishment and was promoted to Direct and Upright Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
s0019.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as a staff officer to the Prince of Nanping and promoted to direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry.

s0020.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace he compiled the Record of the Meaning of the Ever-Spring Hall and had Ling write the preface.
s0020.idiomatic: While Liang's Emperor Jianwen was still in the eastern palace he compiled the Record of the Meaning of the Ever-Spring Hall and had Ling write the preface.

s0021.literal: He also ordered him at the Junior Tutor's office to expound the Zhuangzi commentary he had composed.
s0021.idiomatic: He also had him expound his Zhuangzi commentary at the junior tutor's office.

s0022.literal: Soon he was transferred to Central Secretary to the Prince of Xiangdong, Pacifier of the West.
s0022.idiomatic: Soon he was made central secretary to the Prince of Xiangdong, pacifier of the west.

s0023.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was made Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Scattered Cavalry.
s0023.idiomatic: In Taiqing year 2 (548) he was made concurrent regular attendant of the direct and upright scattered cavalry.

s0024.literal: He was sent on embassy to Wei; the people of Wei lodged him and feasted him as a guest.
s0024.idiomatic: He was sent on embassy to Wei. The Wei lodged him and feasted him as an honored guest.

s0025.literal: That day was very hot; the chief host Wei Shou mocked Ling, saying, "Today's heat must be because Attendant Xu has come.
s0025.idiomatic: That day was fiercely hot. The chief host, Wei Shou, mocked him: "Today's heat must be because Attendant Xu has come.

s0026.literal: " Ling answered at once, "In former days when Wang Su came here, he first gave Wei its rites and ceremonies;
s0026.idiomatic: " Ling answered at once, "When Wang Su came here of old, he first gave Wei its rites and ceremonies;

s0027.literal: now that I have come on embassy, I have let you know again cold and heat.
s0027.idiomatic: now that I have come on embassy, I have taught you again the difference between cold and heat.

s0029.literal: When Hou Jing raided the capital, Ling's father Chi was first inside the besieged city; Ling received no letters from home and at once took to vegetables and plain cloth, as if in mourning and distress.
s0029.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided the capital, Ling's father Chi was trapped inside the siege. Ling received no word from home and at once ate plain food and wore coarse cloth, as though in mourning.

s0030.literal: It happened that Qi received the Mandate from Wei; Emperor Yuan of Liang held provisional rule at Jiangling and again exchanged envoys with Qi.
s0030.idiomatic: Qi then received the mandate from Wei. Emperor Yuan of Liang held provisional rule at Jiangling and again exchanged envoys with Qi.

s0031.literal: Ling repeatedly asked to be sent home with his mission, but in the end was detained and not released; Ling then addressed a letter to the Left Vice Director Yang Zunyian, saying:
s0031.idiomatic: Ling repeatedly asked leave to return with his mission, but was detained and not released. He then wrote to Vice Director Yang Zunyian:

s0032.literal: A single word that moves can make condensed radiance shine on Luoyang; a single will in dark communion can make flying springs gush at Shule—how much more when the head is hale and the limbs good, when neighboring states hear of one another and set their hearts on shared instruction?
s0032.idiomatic: A single word that stirs the heart can hold the sun fast over Luoyang; a single will in hidden accord can make springs burst forth at Shule—how much more when ruler and ministers are sound, when neighboring states hear one another and look to shared teaching?

s0033.literal: Heaven's way is exhausted and stripped; chaos has struck our court. Plans race in panic, public and private alike choke with fear—yet the plea to return home merely drags through a year of cold, and prayers in distress fill scroll after scroll in vain. This is not what I foresaw, nor what I hoped for.
s0033.idiomatic: Heaven's way is stripped bare; chaos has struck our court. In public and private alike fear chokes the throat—yet my plea to go home only drags through another winter, and scrolls of desperate prayer pile up unanswered. I never foresaw this. I never hoped for it.

s0035.literal: In former ages when the tortoise was divided and the pheasant ordained, in years when the river was viewed and Luo received, then there were days of
s0035.idiomatic: In ages when Yu apportioned the turtle and commanded the pheasant, when Tang viewed the river and bowed to the Luo, there came sun-

s0037.literal: Collation variant: [crow]; calamities flowed, Editorial footnote marker 3. wind-birds rampaged wildly, heaven tilted northwest, earth gaped southeast, fierce drought split the three rivers, long waves swallowed the five peaks.
s0037.idiomatic: -calamities in flood, [3] wind-birds rampaged wild, heaven leaned northwest, earth gaped in the southeast, fierce drought split the three rivers, and long waves swallowed the five peaks.

s0038.literal: Our great Liang answered the golden chart yet met with obstruction; it inherited the jade mirror yet still was halted.
s0038.idiomatic: Our great Liang answered the golden chart yet met obstruction; it took up the jade mirror yet still was stalled.

s0040.literal: The sage cannot make the times—this is the constant principle of adversity and success.
s0040.idiomatic: A sage cannot make the times—that is the constant law of rise and fall.

s0041.literal: As for the Governor of Jingzhou, the Prince of Xiangdong—the root of his subtle spirit cannot be lodged in words; what his molding leaves behind is still Yao and Shun. Though the dances of the six dynasties were displayed in the Hall of Total Brilliance and the songs of the nine regions were raised in the Office of Music, though Kui of Yu struck the stone and Kuang of Jin tuned the bell, they would not suffice to praise this heroic renown or declare such overflowing virtue.
s0041.idiomatic: As for the Prince of Xiangdong, governor of Jingzhou—the root of his subtle spirit cannot be put into words; what his molding leaves is still Yao and Shun. Though the dances of six dynasties were set out in the Hall of Total Brilliance and the songs of nine regions were raised in the Office of Music, though Kui of Yu struck stone and Kuang of Jin tuned bells, none of it would suffice to praise his heroic renown or declare such overflowing virtue.

s0042.literal: If suburban sacrifice were offered on Chu wings, would he not be the lord who sacrificed to Xia? If he quelled hardship and danger, he would be the hegemon who restored Zhou—how much less only a King of Bin moving to Yong and making a capital in a month, or Emperor Yao of Yao moving to the river and completing a city in a year.
s0042.idiomatic: If he offered suburban sacrifice on Chu wings, would he not be the lord who restored Xia? If he quelled hardship and danger, he would be the hegemon who righted Zhou—not merely a King of Bin moving to Yong and making a capital in a month, or Emperor Yao of Yao moving to the river and finishing a city in a year.

s0043.literal: Today Yuechang is remote, Editorial footnote marker 4. tame pheasants fly north; Sushen stretches endless, wind and cattle lie south. Sons of our lord who have understanding know where to return—yet your reply asks where we should cast ourselves. This is what I do not understand, the first point.
s0043.idiomatic: Today Yuechang lies far away, [4] tame pheasants fly north; Sushen stretches without end, wind and cattle lie down in the south. Sons of our lord who have sense know where to return—yet your reply asks where we should cast ourselves. That is my first point of doubt.

s0044.literal: Moreover, commanderies such as Jingxi have all entered your honored court; from our Xunyang, how many stages lie on the road?
s0044.idiomatic: Moreover, commanderies such as Jingxi have all entered your honored court. From our Xunyang, how many stages lie on the road?

s0045.literal: As for the clanging dawn watch and the bright night beacons, we hear one another across the Mian ford and can look across from the high tower.
s0045.idiomatic: The clanging dawn watch and the bright night beacons—we hear one another across the Mian ford and can look across from the high tower.

s0046.literal: Springs flow in precious bowls, Editorial footnote marker 5. and from afar we recall Pen city; a peak called Incense Burner—still the Lu Mountains.
s0046.idiomatic: Springs flow in precious bowls, [5] and from afar we recall Pen city; a peak called Incense Burner—still the Lu Mountains.

s0047.literal: Recently the heir prince of Poyang drilled troops where rivers meet and garrisoned the drowned waves; morning and evening he sent memorials, spring and autumn he sent tribute. I have no way to follow in straw sandals—by what road do they keep equal pace?
s0047.idiomatic: Only lately the heir prince of Poyang drilled troops where rivers meet and garrisoned the drowned waves; morning and evening he sent memorials, in spring and autumn he sent tribute. I have no way to follow on foot in straw sandals—by what road do they keep equal pace?

s0050.literal: Moreover, not long ago the Prince of Shaoling made peace with this state; honored guests from Ying gathered like clouds in the Wei capital, famous ministers from Ye raced like wind to the Jiang shore. Has the road through Lulong only now been opened for them, while the Street of Bronze Camels stays long shut for us?
s0050.idiomatic: Moreover, not long ago the Prince of Shaoling made peace with your state: honored guests from Ying gathered like clouds in the Wei capital, famous ministers from Ye raced like wind to the Jiang shore. Has the road through Lulong only now been opened for them, while the Street of Bronze Camels stays long shut for us?

s0051.literal: Why is their road so easy, not laboring the five strong men, while our road is hard, like climbing nine bends?
s0051.idiomatic: Why is their road so easy that it needs no labor of the five strong men, while our road is hard as climbing nine bends?

s0052.literal: Earth does not favor one carriage—how clear is that!
s0052.idiomatic: Earth bears all alike—how plainly fair is that!

s0053.literal: Yet your reply says there is no way home. This is what I do not understand, the second point.
s0053.idiomatic: Yet your reply says there is no way home. That is my second point of doubt.

s0054.literal: Jingxi, Lujiang, Yiyang, and Anlu all say they have submitted in good faith and are no longer perilous states; counting the middle of the road, they should already be calm and settled.
s0054.idiomatic: Jingxi, Lujiang, Yiyang, and Anlu all say they have submitted in good faith and are no longer perilous states; count the middle of the road, and they should already be calm and settled.

s0055.literal: From there northward, drums and rattles do not sound; from here southward, the borders are not yet unified.
s0055.idiomatic: From there northward, drums and rattles do not sound; from here southward, the borders are not yet unified.

s0056.literal: If beyond those borders one should chance to lose one's light body, it would be no shame to a frontier officer—why should a common man's life matter?
s0056.idiomatic: If beyond those borders one should chance to lose one's slight body, it would be no frontier officer's shame—why should a common man's life matter?

s0057.literal: Moreover, on this guest journey Editorial footnote marker 6. there is no trade in goods; I am no Han Qi on embassy to Zheng buying a jade ring in private, no Wu Zha passing through Xu demanding a treasured sword in person.
s0057.idiomatic: Moreover, on this guest journey [6] there is no trade in goods. I am no Han Qi on embassy to Zheng buying a jade ring in private, no Wu Zha passing Xu demanding a treasured sword in person.

s0058.literal: From the first, feasts and gifts—every bag and bundle—through the long delay of travel have all been emptied; scattering limited small funds to supply an endless long stay abroad—this may be known.
s0058.idiomatic: From the first, every feast and gift, every bag and bundle, has been emptied by long delay on the road. I scatter limited small funds to supply an endless stay abroad—that, you may know.

s0059.literal: Moreover, to seize a map and cut one's throat—fools do not do it; to wield an axe and preserve the whole body—even the vulgar take it as a mirror.
s0059.idiomatic: To seize a map and cut one's throat—fools do not do it. To wield an axe and preserve the whole body—even the vulgar take it as a mirror.

s0061.literal: Life is lighter than a single hair, heavier than a thousand jun—this is clear without needing a merchant-thief.
s0061.idiomatic: Life is lighter than a single hair and heavier than a thousand jun—that needs no merchant-thief to make it clear.

s0062.literal: Flesh and bone cannot fill cauldrons and platters; skin and fur are not worth entering as goods for sale. There is a Way even for thieves—I have no worry.
s0062.idiomatic: Flesh and bone cannot fill cauldrons and platters; skin and fur are not worth selling as goods. Even thieves have a Way—I have no worry.

s0063.literal: Moreover, if the government sends envoys and there should be needs, our court is not in a time of great peace, and a traveler cannot bear the majesty of the splendid envoy.
s0063.idiomatic: Moreover, if the government sends envoys and there should be needs, our court is not in a time of great peace, and a traveler cannot bear the majesty of the splendid envoy.

s0064.literal: Light baggage and lodging alone are not the labor of the rite of gathered watch-clappers; a few horsemen traveling at ease cannot look for the ceremony of the envoy's carriage.
s0064.idiomatic: Light baggage and lodging alone are not the labor of the rite of gathered watch-clappers; a few horsemen traveling at ease cannot expect the ceremony of the envoy's carriage.

s0065.literal: Those returning will follow with private donkeys and mules; along the road at post stations I only hope for vegetables and grain.
s0065.idiomatic: Those returning will follow with private donkeys and mules; along the road at post stations I ask only for vegetables and grain.

s0066.literal: If one says that to detain us gives no trouble to the officer in charge, while to send us off costs the government offices, or takes distress as an argument, or says traveling funds are to be feared—that is no proper discussion at all; all are side issues.
s0066.idiomatic: If one says that to detain us gives no trouble to the officer in charge, while to send us off costs the government offices, or takes distress as an argument, or says traveling funds are to be feared—that is no proper discussion at all. All are side issues.

s0067.literal: This is what I do not understand, the third point.
s0067.idiomatic: That is my third point of doubt.

s0068.literal: Moreover, if you say our party ought to return to Hou Jing—Hou Jing is fierce and rebellious and has destroyed our state; all under heaven who have breath harbor indignation. Since we could not throw ourselves into the altars of soil and grain or guard the imperial carriage in peril, we should have the four quarters dismember Chiyou Editorial footnote marker 7. or a thousand blades carve Wang Mang—how then speak of bowing the head and bending the knee to return and serve the bandit foe, wearing bow and sword at the waist to be his menial?
s0068.idiomatic: Moreover, if you say we ought to return to Hou Jing—Hou Jing is fierce and rebellious and has destroyed our state. All who draw breath under heaven harbor rage. We could not throw ourselves on the altars or guard the imperial carriage in peril; we should have had Chiyou torn on four mounds [7] and Wang Mang carved with a thousand blades—how then bow the head, bend the knee, return to serve the bandit foe, and wear bow and sword at the waist as his menial?

s0069.literal: Only lately peace was made and former friendship was thick; the fierce man lay in ambush with deceit and then startled the wolf's heart. I greatly feared the punishment of Song Wan and still more dreaded the plea of Xun Ying—therefore he ran with pounding hooves and sharp horns, indulging his will and lording it over others; every one of us travelers has borne his special hatred.
s0069.idiomatic: Only lately peace was made and old friendship was thick; the fierce man crouched in deceit and then startled the wolf's heart. I feared a punishment like Song Wan's and dreaded still more a plea like Xun Ying's—so he ran with pounding hooves and sharp horns, indulging his will and lording it over all; every traveler in our party has borne his special hatred.

s0070.literal: Even if we were pickled sinew and pounded bone, tongues drawn and livers probed, toward that fierce temper it would still not be enough to clear the score—this is what all within the seas know, and what you, my lord, are fully possessed of.
s0070.idiomatic: Even if we were pickled sinew and pounded bone, tongues drawn and livers probed, toward that fierce temper it would still not clear the score—this all within the seas know, and what you, my lord, are fully possessed of.

s0071.literal: I also hear that the princesses of our court, Editorial footnote marker 8. ladies and women of the capital, were scattered by wind and rain, cast east and west; the capital is a ruin, wanton thickets rustle desolate; looking back on Yanshi, all has become wild grass; turning toward Baling, all are touched by frost and dew—this too is what you know.
s0071.idiomatic: I also hear that the princesses of our court, [8] ladies and women of the capital, were scattered by wind and rain, cast east and west; the capital is a ruin, wanton thickets rustle desolate; looking back on Yanshi, all has become wild grass; turning toward Baling, all are touched by frost and dew—this too you know.

s0072.literal: By what principle do they strive to escape the bandit foe?
s0072.idiomatic: By what principle do they strive to escape the bandit foe?

s0073.literal: By what kinship do I strive to return and submit?
s0073.idiomatic: By what kinship do I strive to return and submit?

s0074.literal: In former days the honored general Juping hung heavy weight on Duke Lu; the famous man Shu Xiang was deeply known by Zong Mie.
s0074.idiomatic: In former days the honored general Juping hung heavy weight on Duke Lu; the famous man Shu Xiang was deeply known by Zong Mie.

s0075.literal: Though I am not clever, I have long admired those earlier exemplars; I did not expect that the enlightened multitude would harbor such feeling yet turn it to measure others in this way.
s0075.idiomatic: Though I am not clever, I have long admired those earlier exemplars. I did not expect that the enlightened multitude would harbor such feeling yet turn it to measure others in this way.

s0076.literal: In former days when the house of Wei was about to perish, many fierce men rose in contention; the worthies joined their strength, thinking to gain their fellowship.
s0076.idiomatic: In former days when the house of Wei was about to perish, many fierce men rose in contention; the worthies joined their strength, thinking to gain their fellowship.

s0077.literal: Are we the party of Ge Rong?
s0077.idiomatic: Are we the party of Ge Rong?

s0078.literal: Are we the followers of Xing Gao?
s0078.idiomatic: Are we the followers of Xing Gao?

s0079.literal: If you say it is not so, this is what I do not understand, the fourth point.
s0079.idiomatic: If you say it is not so, that is my fourth point of doubt.

s0080.literal: Suppose our party did return to the fierce faction: Hou Jing was born in Zhao and Dai; his family came from You and Heng; in residence he was terrace and minister, on campaign he was regional commander; the mountains and rivers, the forms of terrain, the military and civil statutes—without laboring to ask for chopsticks to reckon, he could count them on his fingers.
s0080.idiomatic: Suppose our party did return to the fierce faction: Hou Jing was born in Zhao and Dai; his family came from You and Heng; in residence he was terrace and minister, on campaign he was regional commander; mountains and rivers, terrain, military and civil statutes—without laboring to ask for chopsticks to reckon, he could count them on his fingers.

s0081.literal: Jing was a fugitive petty villain of the same herd as sheep and swine; his person lodged on the river banks, his family remained in Heshuo; bustling and well-ordered, Editorial footnote marker 9. like a ghost, like a god.
s0081.idiomatic: Jing was a fugitive petty villain of the same herd as sheep and swine; his person lodged on the river banks, his family remained in Heshuo; bustling and well-ordered, [9] like a ghost, like a god.

s0083.literal: Or again, this is what you know.

s0084.literal: Moreover, secret affairs of palace and inner quarters are all like clouds in the sky; heroic plans and counsel are surely not outside the command tent—some startled Yang to fix policy, some burned the draft to present the memorial. Men of the court still find it hard to take part; how should a man traveling abroad find a step to ear and eye?
s0084.idiomatic: Moreover, palace secrets are cloud-high; heroic counsel belongs in the command tent—some startled Yang to fix policy, some burned the draft before presenting the memorial. Courtiers still struggle to take part; how should a traveler abroad find a step to ear or eye?

s0085.literal: As for the evolution of rites and music, the leniency or severity of punishments and government—then the songs of praise are already distant, the myriad dances have become custom; one no longer knows that the hands dance them and the feet tread them.
s0085.idiomatic: As for the evolution of rites and music, the leniency or severity of punishments and government—the songs of praise are already distant, the myriad dances have become custom; one no longer knows that the hands dance them and the feet tread them.

s0086.literal: Where is the need to wag one's teeth and be a spy in the gaps?
s0086.idiomatic: Where is the need to wag one's teeth and be a spy in the gaps?

s0087.literal: If you say that on returning to mission for the western court we would in the end flee to the eastern captive—though Qi and Liang are divided, how are the frontier guards different?
s0087.idiomatic: If you say that on returning to mission for the western court we would in the end flee to the eastern captive—though Qi and Liang are divided, how are the frontier guards different?

s0088.literal: How take the difficulty of floating at the river bend and yet say the river passes can be crossed?
s0088.idiomatic: How take the difficulty of floating at the river bend and yet say the river passes can be crossed?

s0089.literal: Horses crossing at the River Bridge—was that not the treachery of Song's canon?
s0089.idiomatic: Horses crossing at the River Bridge—was that not the treachery of Song's canon?

s0090.literal: Cocks crowing on the pass road—all are called the retainers of Tian Wen.
s0090.idiomatic: Cocks crowing on the pass road—all are called the retainers of Tian Wen.

s0091.literal: How penetrating and blind—thus to obstruct one another!
s0091.idiomatic: How penetrating and blind—to obstruct one another so!

s0092.literal: This is what I do not understand, the fifth point.
s0092.idiomatic: That is my fifth point of doubt.

s0093.literal: Moreover, though arms may clash while envoys remain—this is recorded in earlier classics—if it should be like the fault of the servant who died for his master, or the wrath vented on Cold Mountain pursued, then all the commanders would together release bound prisoners, down to junior officers, all alike without cutting down captives.
s0093.idiomatic: Moreover, though arms may clash while envoys remain—this is recorded in earlier classics—if it should be like the fault of the servant who died for his master, or the wrath vented on Cold Mountain pursued, then all the commanders would together release bound prisoners, down to junior officers, all alike without cutting down captives.

s0094.literal: Down to Zhong Yi's being pardoned, Peng's laughter on the road of return; Xiang the elder receiving grace to go home, Yu Ge leading the way.
s0094.idiomatic: Down to Zhong Yi's being pardoned, Peng's laughter on the road of return; Xiang the elder receiving grace to go home, Yu Ge leading the way.

s0095.literal: Editorial footnote marker 10. We have spread banners and wiped jade, repaired good relations and sought alliance; crossing the Si and floating the river, suburban courtesy of labor extending to gifts on departure—your grace has already been shown, guest and host without breach. What fault is there now that we are turned instead to censure?
s0095.idiomatic: [10] We have spread banners and wiped jade, repaired good relations and sought alliance; crossing the Si and floating the river, suburban courtesy of labor extending to gifts on departure—your grace has already been shown, guest and host without breach. What fault is there now that we are turned instead to censure?

s0096.literal: If you take this as your argument, this is what I do not understand, the sixth point.
s0096.idiomatic: If you take this as your argument, that is my sixth point of doubt.

s0097.literal: If you say evil vapors are long-lasting and ruin and chaos stretch on, pity our wandering toil and preserve our bodily souls—we have already engraved this deep kindness and bear this great grace, deep as the Bohai together, heavy still beside Song and Hua.
s0097.idiomatic: If you say evil vapors are long-lasting and ruin and chaos stretch on, pity our wandering toil and preserve our bodily souls—we have already engraved this deep kindness and bear this great grace, deep as the Bohai together, heavy still beside Song and Hua.

s0098.literal: But the beam of the mountain drinks and pecks without intent for cage and fence; rivers and seas float and fly without feeling for bell and drum.
s0098.idiomatic: But the beam of the mountain drinks and pecks without intent for cage and fence; rivers and seas float and fly without feeling for bell and drum.

s0099.literal: Moreover, our camp souls are already spent; remaining breath is left empty; grief and silence are our life—how can we endure long? Thus though we receive fostering care, we shorten our heaven-allotted years.
s0099.idiomatic: Moreover, our camp souls are already spent; remaining breath is left empty; grief and silence are our life—how can we endure long? Thus though we receive fostering care, we shorten our heaven-allotted years.

s0100.literal: If you take this as your argument, this is what I do not understand, the seventh point.
s0100.idiomatic: If you take this as your argument, that is my seventh point of doubt.
